The hint under the Story tables button: what the button is for. It installs the Roleplay story's sentences as Rollable Tables in this world, where the GM can edit them.

column6: The explanation at the top of the Story tables dialog. Every sentence of the Roleplay story is rolled from tables: an action table, named by how it was delivered, the damage type and how well it went (e.g. Melee · Slashing · Minor Success), and a relationship table (e.g. Relationship · Enemy Leader · Failure). Installing them lets the GM edit them, add entries or translate them; tables installed in the world are used before the built-in ones.
column8: Every sentence of the Roleplay story is rolled from a table: an action table (delivery, damage type and how well it went, e.g. Melee · Slashing · Minor Success) plus a relationship table (e.g. Relationship · Enemy Leader · Failure). Install them to edit, add entries or translate; your world tables always win over the built-in ones.

column8: Hidden tokens (ambushers, reinforcements) take part in estimates by default.

column6: The hint under Neutral tokens: what neutral tokens do by default. They stand on the field taking no side, perhaps leaning one way (the choices below). Whoever hurts or robs them, or crosses what they want (hurting someone they lean toward), turns them against their side, and either side's talkers can try to win them over (harder against their lean). The planner's Neutral tab can change it for a battle, and any token can be moved to another side.
column8: Default handling of tokens with Neutral disposition. They stand on the field taking no side, perhaps leaning one way: whoever hurts or robs them, or crosses what they want (hurting someone they lean toward), turns them against their side, and either side's talkers can try to win them over (harder against their lean). Can be changed per battle and per token.

column6: A choice for neutral tokens (this setting's dropdown, and the planner's Neutral tab): they're left out of the fight entirely.
A choice for neutral tokens: on the field, taking no side, leaning nowhere, until something crosses them.
A choice for neutral tokens: taking no side, but leaning toward the party (they want the party's members safe).
A choice for neutral tokens: taking no side, but leaning toward the enemy (they want the enemy's members safe).
A choice for neutral tokens: taking no side, but each leaning toward whichever side is nearest it on the map.
A choice for neutral tokens: taking no side, but leaning toward whichever side is losing (it changes as the fight goes).
A choice for neutral tokens: they fight as a side of their own, against everyone.
